sources.title: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3

control_flags.force: must, or should for a paragraph that says only should but introduces a list of measures (the password-based authentication measures).
control_flags.applies_to: On each theme: the kinds of device and service the theme covers, as printed.
control_flags.objectives: The bulleted items of a requirement, with sub-bullets kept inside their item.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable requirements that are met. Cyber Essentials is pass or fail: certification needs every applicable requirement met. This percentage is an HCG measure of readiness.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.
Certification requires every applicable requirement to be met; there is no partial pass.
rules.quote: You must protect every device in scope with a correctly configured firewall

rules.summary: Critical or high-risk security updates (CVSS v3 7 or above, or where the vendor gives no severity) are applied within 14 days of release.
rules.cite: Cyber Essentials v3.3, Security Update Management
rules.quote: be updated, including vulnerability fixes, within 14 days* of release,

rules.summary: Authentication to cloud services always uses multi-factor authentication.
rules.cite: Cyber Essentials v3.3, User Access Control
rules.quote: authentication to cloud services must always use MFA

glossary.definition: The UK government-backed scheme, run by the NCSC, certifying that an organisation has five basic technical controls in place to protect against common internet-based attacks.
The National Cyber Security Centre, the UK's technical authority for cyber security.
Multi-factor authentication: proving identity with more than one kind of factor, such as a password and a code from a trusted device.
Common Vulnerability Scoring System; Cyber Essentials treats a CVSS v3 base score of 7 or above as critical or high risk.
